title: Has Ford got cheap car fever? A $25K crossover is supposedly on the way.
gist: An unnamed Ford dealer leaked to Automotive News that Ford is developing a roughly $25,000 entry-level crossover for 2029, plus a four-door Mustang priced under $40,000 and four additional EVs off the same universal platform that underpins the sub-$30,000 Fathom electric truck. The context is a US market where average transaction prices crossed $50,000 by the end of last year, leaving only a small handful of new vehicles under $30,000.

insights.claim: Ford is developing an entry-level crossover starting around $25,000, shown to dealers as an early prototype resembling a first-generation Ford Escape, though it will not reach showrooms until 2029.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A three-year lead time means the affordability response is a 2029 story — no near-term volume or margin impact to model.
insights.quote: the automaker is working on a new entry-level crossover that will start at around $25,000, although don’t expect it in showrooms until 2029
insights.locator: Talk of the affordability crisis may be penetrating

insights.claim: The planned entry-level crossover is said to offer both hybrid and non-electrified powertrain options rather than being an EV, indicating Ford's affordability push at the bottom of the range is not electrification-led.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Ford separating cheap from electric implies battery cost still cannot reach a $25k price point even on a 2029 timeline.
insights.quote: The crossover is said to have both hybrid and unelectrified powertrain options
insights.locator: The leak is courtesy of an unnamed Ford dealer

insights.claim: Multiple sources told Automotive News that Ford will build a hybrid crossover at its Hermosillo, Mexico plant in 2029, alongside existing Bronco Sport and Maverick production.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Mexican assembly is the cost mechanism that makes $25k possible — and the tariff exposure that could break it.
insights.locator: Automotive News notes that several sources have told it

insights.claim: Ford also showed dealers a four-door Mustang that Automotive News compares to the Porsche Panamera in size and styling but with a sub-$40,000 price tag — roughly a third the price of the cheapest Panamera.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Stretching the Mustang nameplate into a four-door value sedan is a brand-equity bet that could either expand volume or dilute the marque.
insights.locator: Additionally, Ford apparently showed off a four-door Mustang

insights.claim: The universal electric vehicle platform that underpins the Fathom electric truck will spawn four additional electric Ford models, making platform amortization the core of Ford's low-cost EV strategy.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Five vehicles off one platform is the volume needed to make sub-$30k EV economics work; slippage in any derivative undermines the whole cost case.
insights.quote: the universal electric vehicle platform that will build the Fathom will result in four other electric Ford models as well
insights.locator: And a third nugget of news

insights.claim: US average transaction prices crept above $50,000 by the end of last year, leaving only a relatively small handful of new vehicles purchasable for under $30,000 and fewer still near $25,000.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A $50k ATP against a shrinking sub-$30k shelf is the structural setup for either a low-cost entrant taking share or demand destruction.
insights.quote: average transaction prices* crept above $50,000 by the end of last year, and we’re now left with a relatively small handful of new vehicles that can be purchased for less than $30,000

insights.claim: The industry tracks average transaction price rather than median, a metric choice the author flags as less informative because averages are skewed by high-priced vehicles.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: If ATP overstates what typical buyers pay, the affordability gap may be narrower or wider than headline data suggests — check median where available.
insights.quote: ATP is the statistic that the industry tracks rather than the more potentially informative median

insights.claim: A $25,000 price target quoted in 2029 dollars is materially cheaper in real terms than $25,000 today, meaning the announced figure understates how aggressive the cost engineering must be.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Inflation-adjusting the target raises the odds the car launches above $25k or with content stripped out.
insights.quote: especially if the starting price is about $25,000 in 2029 dollars
insights.locator: So an additional entry to that list ought to be welcome

insights.claim: The author frames affordability pressure as finally reaching corporate boardrooms and explicitly hopes other OEMs follow Ford's lead, implying the low-cost segment has been structurally underserved by the whole industry.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: If Ford's move triggers competitive follow-through, expect industry-wide mix shift downward and pressure on ATP-driven margin assumptions.
insights.quote: Even better would be other OEMs paying attention and following suit.
insights.locator: Talk of the affordability crisis may be penetrating

insights.claim: The entire product roadmap rests on an unnamed Ford dealer's account of a prototype showing, and Ford itself declined to comment or speculate on future products when asked.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Single-source dealer leak with no corporate confirmation — treat pricing and timing as directional intent, not commitment.
insights.quote: Ars reached out to Ford, which told us that it won’t comment or speculate on future products.

insights.claim: The author cautions that a 2029 launch date is far enough out that plenty could change before the small Ford reaches the street, explicitly discounting the reliability of the $25,000 figure.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Long-dated product promises are low-cost signaling; hold judgment until tooling or plant capex is committed.
insights.quote: 2029 is far enough out that plenty could happen to the proposed small Ford before it reaches the streets.
